issues.sym: Without much warning the oil pressure light flickers or comes on, the check engine light shows timing codes such as P0011 or P0021, and the car may drop into limp mode. Oil can also seep from the timing cover.
issues.why: Small rubber gaskets behind the timing cover seal the oil passages that feed the variable valve timing. The early design breaks down, oil pressure leaks away inside the engine, and the cam timing can't be controlled. Nissan revised the gaskets around 2012.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Have a shop that knows this engine confirm the cause. The repair means removing the timing cover, so ask for the updated gaskets.

issues.sym: The oil level drops well before the next change, you may see blue smoke on start-up, and the low oil light can come on.
issues.why: Worn piston rings and valve seals on the 4.5L V8 let oil into the cylinders. Owners of 2004 and 2006 M45s report repairs from a few thousand dollars up to an engine replacement.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it topped off so the timing chain and bearings aren't starved. Ask a shop to run an oil consumption test before deciding on repairs.

issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the car, then a sudden loss of drive power. With a broken driveshaft the car can also roll away in Park if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: The driveshaft on rear-wheel-drive versions can fatigue and crack. Recalls cover 2011-2013 M56, 2012-2013 M35 Hybrid, and 2014-2019 Q70, Q70L and Q70 Hybrid with two-wheel drive.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the driveshaft for free.

issues.sym: No warning sign. The risk shows up in a crash that sets off the front passenger airbag.
issues.why: The Takata passenger airbag inflator can break down over years of heat and humidity and burst when it deploys, throwing metal pieces into the cabin. Several recalls cover 2006-2010 M35 and M45, including replacement parts used in earlier repairs.
issues.next: Check your VIN with Infiniti or NHTSA now, even if the car had an earlier airbag recall. The repair is free.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal sensor can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Limp mode with very little power, a check engine light, or stalling at idle or low speed.
issues.why: The sensor inside the accelerator pedal can wear and send bad signals. The engine computer then goes into a fail-safe mode, and throttle deposits can make it stall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer replaces the pedal assembly and reprograms the engine computer for free.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensor nut corrodes and leaks air (recall)
issues.sym: A tire slowly loses air and the tire pressure light comes on.
issues.why: In heavy road-salt states the nut holding the tire pressure sensor to the wheel can corrode and crack, letting air leak out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer fits a stronger nut for free.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads full when the tank is low (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows more fuel than is in the tank, and the car can run out of gas and stall.
issues.why: A circuit board fault in the fuel gauge system makes it read high.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups until it is fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer modifies the circuit board for free.

issues.t: Crank or cam sensor can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, a no-start, low power or stalling.
issues.why: Bad solder joints on the circuit board inside the crankshaft or camshaft position sensors.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the sensors for free.

issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine, louder when cold, and sometimes an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifolds on the first M45's V8 crack from repeated heating and cooling. It is the most-reported problem on the 2003 M45.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the manifold replaced with new studs and gaskets.

issues.t: Driver's seat track or frame breaks
issues.sym: The driver's seat rocks, tilts back or comes loose, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: Owners report broken seat frames on the 2003 M45 and broken seat tracks on the 2006 M35, often around 70,000-85,000 miles. The repair is often costly.
issues.next: If the seat moves or feels loose, don't drive until it is repaired. A dealer or upholstery shop can replace the track or frame.

issues.t: Passenger airbag light from seat sensor fault
issues.sym: The airbag warning light or passenger airbag off light stays on, even with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The weight sensor in the passenger seat or its control unit fails. Owners report repairs can be expensive, and some sensor parts are now discontinued.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The passenger airbag may not deploy while the light is on, so get it fixed. Ask about a used or rebuilt sensor if new parts aren't available.

issues.sym: The dashboard top cracks, bubbles or gets sticky, and can glare in the windshield.
issues.why: The dash material breaks down with heat and sunlight.
issues.next: Use a sunshade. A dash cover hides the damage; replacing the dash pad is costly.

issues.t: Groaning from the steering rack on AWD models
issues.sym: A groan or moan when turning the wheel, especially at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a groaning steering rack as the most common M35 problem on all-wheel-drive cars. Low or worn power steering fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid. If the noise continues with the fluid full, have the pump and rack inspected; a worn rack may need replacing.

issues.sym: Idle speed dips very low, the engine shakes, or it stalls when stopping.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a stall or low idle condition for the M35. Carbon on the throttle body and a lost idle setting are common causes, and the accelerator pedal sensor recall can also cause it.
issues.next: Check for the pedal recall first. Then have the throttle body cleaned and an idle relearn done.

issues.sym: A sweet antifreeze smell, falling coolant level, or coolant drips at the front of the car.
issues.why: Owners report an antifreeze smell on a nearly new 2012 M37 and a leaking radiator O-ring at about 96,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested and fix leaks early to avoid overheating.

issues.t: Side mirrors tilt down by themselves
issues.sym: The outside mirrors move to the down position on their own, now and then.
issues.why: The mirror memory or reverse tilt-down function can act up from a switch or module glitch.
issues.next: Have the mirror memory settings and switch checked. A reset or switch replacement usually fixes it.

issues.t: Hands-free calls: other person hears whistling or nothing
issues.sym: On Bluetooth calls the other person can't hear you, or hears a whistling sound.
issues.why: Infiniti issued bulletins for these hands-free phone problems; the fix is reprogramming or reconfiguring the system.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply bulletins ITB12-063 and ITB18-042.

issues.sym: Cruise control won't engage and a P0605 code is stored.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB13-13 covers this; the engine computer logs an internal fault code.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light from an EVAP tube leak
issues.sym: Check engine light for an evaporative emissions leak.
issues.why: Infiniti extended warranty coverage on an EVAP tube on these cars.
issues.next: Ask a dealer if your VIN is covered before paying for the repair.

issues.t: Front parking sensors beep with nothing there
issues.sym: The front sonar warns of an obstacle when nothing is in front of the car.
issues.why: Infiniti's bulletin found the license plate, frame or bracket can trigger the front sensor.
issues.next: Check the front plate and bracket for interference; a dealer can follow bulletin ITB16-006.

issues.sym: A shudder or vibration when the car shifts or pulls away.
issues.why: Owners of 2015 Q70s report shudder from the 7-speed automatic; the exact cause varies from car to car.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned and the fluid checked. Ask about software updates for the transmission computer.

issues.sym: The forward collision braking system brakes when it shouldn't, or warns and doesn't work as expected.
issues.why: Owners of 2015 Q70s report the automatic braking system not working properly. The system depends on a front radar sensor that must be clean and correctly aimed.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor area clean. If it misbehaves, have the radar checked and aimed by a dealer.

issues.t: Hesitation or low power after a cold start
issues.sym: The car feels sluggish or hesitates when you first pull away in the morning, or when you try to pass.
issues.why: Infiniti issued bulletin ITB19-004 for lack of power after a cold soak on 2019 V6 Q70s, and owners report hesitation that dealers struggled to fix.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply bulletin ITB19-004 and the related engine computer update (ITB20-013).

issues.t: Check engine light with code P0315
issues.sym: Check engine light on with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB19-045 covers code P0315, a crankshaft position learning code.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to follow the bulletin; it usually needs a relearn, not new parts.

issues.sym: The car won't start, especially after sitting.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB19-034 covers no-start conditions from low battery voltage.
issues.next: Test and charge the battery, then ask the dealer about the bulletin if it repeats.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be switched off (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen stays blank in reverse.
issues.why: The display settings could turn off the rear camera image and keep it off the next time you reverse.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer updates the software for free.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a whine, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump on the 3.7L V6 typically wears out around 100,000 miles and starts to leak from its seal.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. Replace the pump at the first sign of leaking to avoid overheating.

issues.sym: Check engine light, misfires, a rattle from the exhaust, rough idle and poor power.
issues.why: High exhaust temperatures can break up the honeycomb inside the converters on the 3.7L V6, sometimes as early as 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Fix any misfire right away. Have exhaust back-pressure checked if power drops.

issues.sym: The sunroof glass suddenly breaks with a bang, often while driving, leaving glass in the cabin.
issues.why: RepairPal lists exploding sunroofs as a reported Q70 problem and points to possible manufacturing issues with the glass.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Keep the broken glass and photos, report it to NHTSA, and ask Infiniti for goodwill help with the replacement.

issues.sym: Air comes out of the wrong vents, temperature won't change, or you hear clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: RepairPal owners report HVAC actuators that fail or work only some of the time, upsetting airflow and temperature control.
issues.next: Have a shop scan the climate system and find which actuator has failed. Replacing one actuator is usually a modest job.

issues.t: Emergency call and connected services stop working
issues.sym: The SOS button and connected services stop working or show an error.
issues.why: The cars' telematics unit used older cellular networks that were shut down. Infiniti ran campaigns to replace or deactivate the hardware.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether a telematics campaign applies to your VIN.
